evidence: Mart. 1.15.12: sēra nimis vīta est crāstina
terms.comment: Before adjectives and adverbs (nimis graviter, too harshly: Ter. Heaut. 5.5.1, Lewis & Short); with a genitive, too much of (nimis īnsidiārum: Cic. Or. 170). Nōn nimis is “not very” (Cic. Att. 7.24.1, Lewis & Short). Latin often says “too” with the comparative alone: sērius, too late (Traupman 87); pede major, too big for the foot (see too big).
The same word as nimis, in all its uses (Lewis & Short); as a noun with a genitive, too much: nimium est aquae, there’s too much water.

phrases.latin: nōn est, crēde mihi, sapientis dīcere "vīvam": sēra nimis vīta est crāstina: vīve hodiē
phrases.english: believe me, it is not wise to say ‘I shall live’: tomorrow’s life is too late; live today

phrases.latin: nunc quidem etiam nimium est aquae
phrases.english: just now there’s even too much water
